records.source: בְּיָמָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיְהִי־ל֨וֹ יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים עֶ֨בֶד֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיִּמְרָד־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: In his days came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and became to him Jehoiakim [a] servant three years; and he turned and rebelled against him.
pieces: In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his vassal for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

L.1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant [for] three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.

R.1: While Jehoiakim was king, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the land. For three years Jehoiakim had to serve him. Then Jehoiakim turned against him and rebelled.

decisions.choice: in his days: during the reign of Jehoiakim, when Babylon took over from Egypt
decisions.reason: "His" is Jehoiakim, whose reign began in 23:36. Pharaoh Neco had put him on the throne and made him pay tribute (23:34-35). Babylon then defeated Egypt at Carchemish on the Euphrates in the fourth year of Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 46:2), about 605 BC, and Nebuchadnezzar came west to claim the lands Egypt had held (verse 7). This is the first time Kings names him.

decisions.choice: servant: a vassal king, ruling under Babylon and paying it tribute
decisions.reason: The word for a slave or servant is used of a whole king or people that is subject to a stronger king (17:3; 18:7). Jehoiakim kept his throne but owed Nebuchadnezzar loyalty and yearly payments.

decisions.choice: he turned and rebelled: he changed course and threw off Babylon's rule
decisions.reason: The verb "turned" before another verb marks a change of direction: after three years of submission Jehoiakim reversed his policy. To rebel against a king is to refuse him the tribute and loyalty owed (18:7).

decisions.choice: vassal (Balanced); had to serve him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servant". Here the word names a subject king, not a household servant or a court official, so Balanced says "vassal" and Readable says what that meant for Jehoiakim. Balanced names Jehoiakim for "his days" so the reader knows whose reign is meant.

records.heading: Jehoiakim and Babylon

records.source: וַיְשַׁלַּ֣ח יְהוָ֣ה׀בּ֡וֹ אֶת־גְּדוּדֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּים֩ וְאֶת־גְּדוּדֵ֨י אֲרָ֜ם וְאֵ֣ת׀גְּדוּדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֗ב וְאֵת֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֔וֹן וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥ם בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה לְהַֽאֲבִיד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
records.gloss: And sent Yahweh against him bands of Chaldeans and bands of Aram and bands of Moab and bands of [the] sons of Ammon, and he sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of his servants the prophets.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites against him. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, in keeping with the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

L.2: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent against him raiding bands of [the] Chaldeans and raiding bands of Aram and raiding bands of Moab and raiding bands of the sons of Ammon; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the prophets.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent bands of raiders against Jehoiakim: Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites. He sent them to attack Judah and destroy it. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

decisions.choice: Yahweh sent them: the raids were Yahweh's doing
decisions.reason: The verse says twice that Yahweh sent the raiders. The attacks of the neighboring peoples are told as his judgment on Judah, not only as border warfare after Jehoiakim's rebellion.

decisions.choice: Chaldeans, Aram, Moab, the sons of Ammon: Babylon's forces and Judah's neighbors
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings, Nebuchadnezzar among them, now ruled Babylon. Aram lay to the north-east of Israel, and Moab and Ammon east of the Jordan; all three were under Babylon's control and joined in harassing Judah. A raiding band is a troop that strikes and plunders, not a full army.

decisions.choice: to destroy it: Judah
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular and points back to Judah. The raids were meant to bring Judah to ruin, not only to punish its king.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh spoken through his servants the prophets
decisions.reason: Under Manasseh, Yahweh had said through his servants the prophets that he would bring disaster on Jerusalem and Judah and hand them over to their enemies (21:10-15). Huldah repeated it to Josiah (22:16-17).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 17:13: "slave" at Literal and "servant" at Balanced and Readable for those who belong to Yahweh and speak for him.

decisions.choice: Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the peoples rather than their lands ("bands of Aram", "of Moab", "of the sons of Ammon"), and say "raiding bands" once for all four. Readable names Jehoiakim for "him".

records.source: אַ֣ךְ׀עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה לְהָסִ֖יר מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו בְּחַטֹּ֣את מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: Surely at [the] mouth of Yahweh it came against Judah, to remove [them] from before his face, because of [the] sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did,
pieces: Surely it was at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that this came upon Judah, to put them away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence because of Manasseh's sins, all that he had done,

L.3: Surely at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} this came upon Judah, to remove [them] from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,

R.3: This happened to Judah because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded it. He was going to send the people away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence because of the sins of Manasseh and all the evil he had done.

decisions.choice: surely: this happened in fact, and for this reason
decisions.reason: The opening word stresses what follows. It can also mean "only", which would give "only at Yahweh's command"; either way the point is that the disaster did not come by chance but at Yahweh's word.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: What comes from someone's mouth is their order. Yahweh had spoken, and what he said now came about (verse 2).

decisions.choice: to remove from before his face: to drive Judah out of the land where Yahweh is present
decisions.reason: To remove from Yahweh's face is to send away from his presence, from the land and the temple where he had put his name. The same words were used of the northern kingdom's exile (17:18, 23) and of Yahweh's decision about Judah (23:27). "Them" is supplied: the people of Judah.

decisions.choice: because of the sins of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Manasseh rebuilt the high places, set up altars to the host of heaven in the temple courts and made his son pass through the fire (21:2-9). Even Josiah's reform did not turn back Yahweh's anger over what Manasseh had done (23:26). The sentence continues in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Surely it was at the command of ... that; because ... commanded it
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the stress where the Hebrew does, on Yahweh's command, with an English "it was ... that". Readable makes the command the reason and ends the sentence early, naming "the people" as those sent away.

records.source: וְגַ֤ם דַּֽם־הַנָּקִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁפָ֔ךְ וַיְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑י וְלֹֽא־אָבָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לִסְלֹֽחַ׃
records.gloss: and also [the] blood of the innocent which he shed, and he filled Jerusalem [with] innocent blood, and not was willing Yahweh to forgive.
pieces: and also because of the innocent blood he had shed. He had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not willing to forgive.

L.4: and also the innocent blood that he had shed; for he filled Jerusalem [with] innocent blood, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not willing to forgive.

R.4: Manasseh had also killed many innocent people. He filled Jerusalem with their blood, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would not forgive that.

decisions.choice: shed innocent blood: put to death people who had done nothing to deserve it
decisions.reason: Blood stands for a life taken by violence. Innocent blood is the blood of people killed unjustly, which the law said defiles the land and cries out for justice (Deuteronomy 19:10; 21:8-9).

decisions.choice: he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood
decisions.reason: These are almost the words of 21:16, which says Manasseh shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was not willing to forgive
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Yahweh's pardon. Here Yahweh refuses it: the guilt of Manasseh's reign remained on Jerusalem and was not taken away, even by Josiah's reform (23:26). The verb means unwilling, not unable.

decisions.choice: had also killed many innocent people
decisions.reason: Readable says what shedding innocent blood means and names Manasseh, since Readable ended the sentence at verse 3. "Many" stands for filling the city with blood.

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוֹיָקִ֖ים וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jehoiakim and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.

L.5: And the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

R.5: Everything else Jehoiakim did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: a royal record the writer could consult
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Kings (12:20; 1 Kings 15:7), the writer sends the reader to a fuller written record of Judah's kings, now lost. The question "are they not written ...?" means "they are written".

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in the sources formula throughout these books, Balanced and Readable state as a fact what the Hebrew asks as a question; Literal keeps the question.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב יְהוֹיָקִ֖ים עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And lay down Jehoiakim with his fathers, and reigned Jehoiachin his son in his place.
pieces: Jehoiakim rested with his ancestors, and his son Jehoiachin became king in his place.

L.6: And Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

R.6: Jehoiakim died, and his son Jehoiachin became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: he died; no burial is mentioned
decisions.reason: The usual formula for a king's death is followed here without the usual note of his burial. Jeremiah had said Jehoiakim would not be mourned and would have "the burial of a donkey", dragged out beyond the gates (Jeremiah 22:18-19; 36:30). 2 Chronicles 36:6 says Nebuchadnezzar bound him in bronze chains to take him to Babylon. The text does not say how these accounts fit together.

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin: also called Jeconiah and Coniah
decisions.reason: The name means "Yahweh will establish". Other books call the same king Jeconiah (1 Chronicles 3:16; Jeremiah 24:1) and Coniah (Jeremiah 22:24), shorter or reordered forms of the same name. Every level keeps the form this verse uses.

decisions.choice: rested with his ancestors (Balanced); died (Readable)
decisions.reason: The death formula as in the rest of Kings. Readable says only "died" because the verse names no burial.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־הֹסִ֥יף עוֹד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָצֵ֖את מֵֽאַרְצ֑וֹ כִּֽי־לָקַ֞ח מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֗ל מִנַּ֤חַל מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־נְהַר־פְּרָ֔ת כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיְתָ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: And not again did come out again [the] king of Egypt from his land, for had taken [the] king of Babylon, from [the] wadi of Egypt to [the] river Euphrates, all that had belonged to [the] king of Egypt.
pieces: The king of Egypt did not again march out from his own land, for the king of Babylon had taken everything that had belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River.

L.7: And the king of Egypt did not again come out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken, from the Wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates, all that had belonged to the king of Egypt.

R.7: The king of Egypt never again led his army out of his own country. The king of Babylon had taken over all the land the king of Egypt had ruled, from the Wadi of Egypt in the south to the Euphrates River in the north.

decisions.choice: the king of Egypt did not come out again: Egypt no longer campaigned in the region
decisions.reason: Pharaoh Neco had marched to the Euphrates, killed Josiah and set Judah's kings on and off the throne (23:29-35). After Babylon's victory at Carchemish (Jeremiah 46:2) Egypt kept its army at home, so Jehoiakim's rebellion (verse 1) had no ally to rely on.

decisions.choice: from the Wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates: the whole land between Egypt and Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: The Wadi of Egypt is the dry stream bed at the southwest edge of Canaan (1 Kings 8:65), and the Euphrates the great river to the north-east. These were also the limits of Solomon's rule (1 Kings 5:1; 8:65), and now all of it was Babylon's.

decisions.choice: for ... had taken: the reason Egypt stayed home
decisions.reason: The second clause explains the first: Babylon had already taken the territory, so Egypt had nothing left to march into. The verb points to a past action completed before Jehoiakim's death.

decisions.choice: march out (Balanced); led his army out (Readable); Wadi of Egypt
decisions.reason: "Come out" here means to go out to war, and Balanced and Readable say so. "Wadi of Egypt" is kept as in 1 Kings 8:65, a wadi being a stream bed that is dry except in the rainy season; Readable adds "in the south" and "in the north" to show the span of the land.

records.source: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נְחֻשְׁתָּ֥א בַת־אֶלְנָתָ֖ן מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: [A] son of eighteen year[s] [was] Jehoiachin when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
pieces: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

L.8: A son of eighteen years [was] Jehoiachin when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

R.8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a son of eighteen years: eighteen years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the son of so many years (12:1).

decisions.choice: eighteen years old, three months: 2 Chronicles 36:9 has eight years, and adds ten days
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 36:9 says Jehoiachin was eight years old and reigned three months and ten days. Kings says eighteen, and the mention of his wives in verse 15 fits the older age. The figure in Chronicles may come from a copying slip; some ancient translations of Chronicles have eighteen.

decisions.choice: Nehushta: the queen mother, who shared his fate
decisions.reason: For the kings of Judah the formula names the king's mother, who held a place of her own at court. Nehushta surrendered and went into exile with her son (verses 12, 15; Jeremiah 13:18; 22:26). Her father Elnathan may be the Elnathan son of Achbor who served Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 26:22; 36:12), but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the age as English does and put the name first; Literal keeps the Hebrew order and idiom.

records.heading: Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done his father.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his father had done.

L.9: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that his father had done.

R.9: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as his father had done.

decisions.choice: the verdict on the king: he followed his father Jehoiakim
decisions.reason: Kings judges every king by his faithfulness to Yahweh. Jehoiachin is given the same verdict as his father (23:37). His reign was too short for the writer to name particular deeds.

decisions.choice: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: The fixed wording for this formula at each level: "did the evil in [the] eyes of", "did what was evil in the sight of", "did what the LORD said was evil".

records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא עָל֗וּ עַבְדֵ֛י נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: At the time the that went up [the] servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon [to] Jerusalem, and came the city into the siege.
pieces: At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon advanced on Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

L.10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up [to] Jerusalem, and the city came into siege.

R.10: At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem. They surrounded the city and attacked it.

decisions.choice: went up: the plural form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have the singular "he went up"; the scribes marked the plural "they went up" to be read aloud (qere), agreeing with "the servants". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the servants of Nebuchadnezzar: his officers and the troops under them
decisions.reason: A king's servants are the men who act for him. Here they are his army commanders, who began the siege before the king himself arrived (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the city came into siege: Jerusalem was surrounded and cut off
decisions.reason: To come into siege is to be shut in by an enemy army camped around the walls, so that no one can go in or out and food runs short.

decisions.choice: officers
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servants". For a king's men acting for him, Balanced and Readable may say "officials"; here they lead an army, so both say "officers". Readable says what the siege meant in two plain verbs.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֛א נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל עַל־הָעִ֑יר וַעֲבָדָ֖יו צָרִ֥ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon against the city, and his servants [were] besieging it.
pieces: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city himself while his officers were besieging it.

L.11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, while his servants were besieging it.

R.11: Then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city himself while his officers were attacking it.

decisions.choice: his servants besieging it: what was going on when the king arrived
decisions.reason: The second clause uses a participle with no main verb: the siege was already in progress, and the king came to it. The king's coming marks the decisive stage of the siege.

decisions.choice: himself; officers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "himself" to bring out the contrast with his officers in verse 10, and keep "officers" as in verse 10.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֞א יְהוֹיָכִ֤ין מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל ה֣וּא וְאִמּ֔וֹ וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְשָׂרָ֣יו וְסָֽרִיסָ֑יו וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁמֹנֶ֖ה לְמָלְכֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And went out Jehoiachin king of Judah to [the] king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his princes and his eunuchs; and took him [the] king of Babylon in [the] year eight of his reigning.
pieces: Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon in surrender, he and his mother, his servants, his officials and his court officers. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.

L.12: And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother and his servants and his princes and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him in [the] eighth year of his reign.

R.12: Jehoiachin king of Judah surrendered to the king of Babylon. He went out to him with his mother, his servants, his leaders and his palace officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner. It was the eighth year that Nebuchadnezzar had been king.

decisions.choice: went out to the king of Babylon: surrendered
decisions.reason: To go out of a besieged city to the enemy king is to give oneself up to him (18:31; 1 Samuel 11:3). Jehoiachin came out with his whole court.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal officials, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: The word names a class of court officers. Many of them in the courts of the ancient Near East were castrated, but the word is also used of high officials who were not, so it may simply mean "palace officials" here.

decisions.choice: the eighth year of his reign: Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year, 597 BC
decisions.reason: "His" is the king of Babylon. Babylon's own records of the period date the capture of Jerusalem to early 597 BC. Jeremiah 52:28 dates a deportation to Nebuchadnezzar's seventh year; that list may count the years from a different starting point, or describe another group.

decisions.choice: took him: the start of Jehoiachin's long captivity
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin stayed a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years, until a later king of Babylon released him (25:27-30).

decisions.choice: servants, princes, eunuchs (Literal); servants, officials, court officers (Balanced); servants, leaders, palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: Three words for the king's court stand side by side here. Literal follows the usual wording for each. Balanced uses "officials" for the princes as usual, so it calls the eunuchs "court officers" to keep the three groups apart; Readable has "leaders" for the princes and "palace officials" for the eunuchs.

decisions.choice: in surrender; took him prisoner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what going out to the enemy and being taken meant. Readable names Nebuchadnezzar so that "his reign" is clear.

records.source: וַיּוֹצֵ֣א מִשָּׁ֗ם אֶת־כָּל־אוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֽוֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְקַצֵּ֞ץ אֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he brought out from there all [the] treasures of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasures of [the] house of the king, and he cut up all [the] vessels of the gold which had made Solomon king of Israel in [the] temple of Yahweh, as had spoken Yahweh.
pieces: He carried off from there all the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and those of the king's palace, and he cut up all the gold vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

L.13: And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasures of the house of the king, and he cut up all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken.

R.13: Nebuchadnezzar took away all the treasures from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the king's palace. He cut into pieces all the gold objects that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had spoken: through Isaiah to Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah had told Hezekiah that everything in his palace and all his ancestors had stored up would be carried off to Babylon (20:17). Temple treasure had been handed over before to buy off enemies (12:19; 18:15-16) and seized in war (14:14), but now Babylon took it all.

decisions.choice: cut up: broke the gold vessels into pieces or stripped off their gold
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off or cut into pieces. It was used when Hezekiah stripped the gold from the temple doors (18:16). The gold was taken as metal, not kept as vessels. Some of Solomon's bronze furnishings were left until the city's fall (25:13-17).

decisions.choice: the vessels of gold that Solomon had made
decisions.reason: Solomon's gold furnishings for the temple are listed in 1 Kings 7:48-51.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Readable names the king for "he", and leaves out the second "of the LORD" after "temple", which is clear from the first.

records.source: וְהִגְלָ֣ה אֶת־כָּל־יְ֠רוּשָׁלִַם וְֽאֶת־כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֞ים וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַחַ֗יִל עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ גּוֹלֶ֔ה וְכָל־הֶחָרָ֖שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּ֑ר לֹ֣א נִשְׁאַ֔ר זוּלַ֖ת דַּלַּ֥ת עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And he exiled all Jerusalem and all the princes and all [the] mighty [men] of the valor, ten thousand exiles, and every craftsman and the smith; not was left except [the] poorest of [the] people of the land.
pieces: He carried all Jerusalem into exile: all the officials and all the mighty warriors, 10,000 captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths. No one was left except the poorest people of the land.

L.14: And he exiled all Jerusalem and all the princes and all the mighty men of valor, 10,000 exiles, and every craftsman and smith; none was left except the poorest of the people of the land.

R.14: He took the people of Jerusalem away as captives. He took all the leaders and all the best soldiers, 10,000 people in all, and all the skilled workers and metalworkers. Only the poorest people in the land were left.

decisions.choice: ten: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a different form of the number ten; the scribes marked the usual form to be read aloud (qere). The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: all Jerusalem: the city's leading people, not every person
decisions.reason: The verse itself says the poorest were left, and Jerusalem still had a king and people under Zedekiah (verses 17-20; 25:11). "All Jerusalem" means the city as a community, and the lists that follow say who was taken.

decisions.choice: smith: a metalworker, though the exact trade is uncertain
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to shut" or "to close". It may name smiths, makers of locks and fittings, or men who built or held fortifications. Taking away the craftsmen left Judah unable to make weapons or repair its walls.

decisions.choice: ten thousand exiles: a total, probably counted with the groups of verse 16
decisions.reason: Verse 16 counts seven thousand fighting men and a thousand craftsmen. The ten thousand here may include them, together with the officials and the court, or the two verses may give two separate counts. Jeremiah 52:28 gives 3,023 people of Judah taken in Nebuchadnezzar's seventh year, perhaps counting only one group.

decisions.choice: the poorest of the people of the land
decisions.reason: Those left were the poor who had no land, rank or skill that mattered to Babylon. The same happened after the city's fall (25:12).

decisions.choice: officials, mighty warriors (Balanced); leaders, best soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The princes are "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable, as in these books. "Mighty men of valor" are fighting men known for their strength and courage; Balanced says "mighty warriors" and Readable "best soldiers".

records.source: וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת־יְהוֹיָכִ֖ין בָּבֶ֑לָה וְאֶת־אֵ֣ם הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וְאֶת־סָרִיסָ֗יו וְאֵת֙ אֵילֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹלִ֛יךְ גּוֹלָ֥ה מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon, and [the] mother of the king and [the] wives of the king and his eunuchs and [the] leaders of the land he led [into] exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
pieces: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon. The king's mother, the king's wives, his court officers and the leading men of the land he also took into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

L.15: And he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon; and the mother of the king and the wives of the king and his eunuchs and the leading men of the land he led away [into] exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

R.15: Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin to Babylon as a captive. He also took the king's mother, his wives, his palace officials and the most important men of the land. He carried them all away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

decisions.choice: the leading men: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) spell the word differently; the scribes marked this form to be read aloud (qere). Both name the powerful men of the land.

decisions.choice: the leading men of the land: its powerful and wealthy men
decisions.reason: The word can mean rams, the strong leaders of a flock, and is used of chiefs and nobles (Exodus 15:15; Ezekiel 17:13). With the court, they made up Judah's ruling class.

decisions.choice: he exiled Jehoiachin to Babylon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that Coniah (Jehoiachin) and his mother would be thrown into a land where they were not born (Jeremiah 22:24-27). His letter to the exiles names this same group: the king, the queen mother, the court officials and the princes (Jeremiah 29:2). Ezekiel was among those taken, and dated his book by this exile (Ezekiel 1:2).

decisions.choice: court officers (Balanced); palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12. Readable says "most important men" for the leading men of the land and names Nebuchadnezzar for "he".

records.source: וְאֵת֩ כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֗ים וְהֶחָרָ֤שׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר֙ אֶ֔לֶף הַכֹּ֕ל גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים עֹשֵׂ֣י מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל גּוֹלָ֖ה בָּבֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] men of the valor, seven thousand, and the craftsman and the smith, a thousand, the all [were] mighty, makers of war, and brought them [the] king of Babylon [as] exiles to Babylon.
pieces: The king of Babylon brought to Babylon as exiles all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and smiths, a thousand, all of them strong men fit for war.

L.16: And all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand, all [of them] mighty, makers of war, the king of Babylon brought them [as] exiles to Babylon.

R.16: The king of Babylon also took to Babylon as captives 7,000 of the best fighting men and a thousand skilled workers and metalworkers. All of them were strong and able to fight.

decisions.choice: men of valor: able fighting men
decisions.reason: The word for valor also means strength, ability and wealth, and "men of valor" can mean men of standing. Next to "makers of war" it means men able to fight.

decisions.choice: all of them mighty, makers of war: said of the whole group
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe all eight thousand, or only the craftsmen, who were strong men who could also serve in war. Either way, Babylon took the men who could have defended or rebuilt Judah.

decisions.choice: seven thousand ... a thousand: counts within the exile of verse 14
decisions.reason: See verse 14 on how these numbers relate to the ten thousand there.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the groups first and then says "the king of Babylon brought them". Balanced and Readable start with the king, as English does; Readable keeps "metalworkers" for the smiths as in verse 14.

records.source: וַיַּמְלֵ֧ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־מַתַּנְיָ֥ה דֹד֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And made king [the] king of Babylon Mattaniah his uncle in his place, and he changed his name [to] Zedekiah.
pieces: The king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.

L.17: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place, and he changed his name [to] Zedekiah.

R.17: The king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king in his place. He changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.

decisions.choice: his uncle: Jehoiachin's father's brother
decisions.reason: Mattaniah was a son of Josiah and a brother of Jehoiakim (1 Chronicles 3:15; Jeremiah 1:3). 2 Chronicles 36:10 calls him Jehoiachin's "brother", using the word in its wider sense of a male relative.

decisions.choice: he changed his name: a sign of the overlord's power
decisions.reason: Renaming a king showed who had made him king and whom he served, as when Pharaoh Neco renamed Eliakim Jehoiakim (23:34). Mattaniah means "gift of Yahweh"; Zedekiah means "Yahweh is my righteousness" or "Yahweh is righteous". Both names honor Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Mattaniah, Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Each level keeps both names in the data's English forms. Balanced and Readable name Jehoiachin for "his" so it is clear whose uncle Mattaniah was, and Readable names Mattaniah for the second "his".

records.source: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה׃
records.gloss: [A] son of twenty and one year[s] [was] Zedekiah when he became king, and one [and] ten year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
pieces: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

L.18: A son of twenty-one years [was] Zedekiah when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

R.18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:1 and in 2 Chronicles 36:11
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 are repeated almost word for word in Jeremiah 52:1-3, which begins that book's account of Jerusalem's fall. 2 Chronicles 36:11 gives the same age and length of reign but leaves out his mother.

decisions.choice: Hamutal: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) spell the name Hamital; the scribes marked Hamutal to be read aloud (qere), the form used in 23:31. It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah: also the mother of Jehoahaz
decisions.reason: Hamutal was the mother of Jehoahaz as well (23:31), so Zedekiah was his full brother and a half brother of Jehoiakim. Her father Jeremiah of Libnah, a town in the lowland of Judah, is not the prophet Jeremiah, who came from Anathoth (Jeremiah 1:1).

decisions.choice: eleven years: from 597 BC to the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Zedekiah reigned until the city fell in his eleventh year (25:2), about 586 BC.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old
decisions.reason: As in verse 8: Balanced and Readable give the age as English does and put the name first.

records.heading: Zedekiah king of Judah

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done Jehoiakim.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as Jehoiakim had done.

L.19: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

R.19: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as Jehoiakim had done.

decisions.choice: according to all that Jehoiakim had done: measured against his brother
decisions.reason: Zedekiah is compared with his brother Jehoiakim, not with his father Josiah. The book of Jeremiah shows him unwilling to heed the prophet's word even when he asked for it (Jeremiah 37-38). Jeremiah 52:2 has the same words.

decisions.choice: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.source: כִּ֣י׀עַל־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּבִ֣יהוּדָ֔ה עַד־הִשְׁלִכ֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃ס
records.gloss: For on [the] anger of Yahweh it happened in Jerusalem and in Judah, until he cast them from on his face; and rebelled Zedekiah against [the] king of Babylon.
pieces: It was because of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

L.20: For because of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} it came to be in Jerusalem and in Judah, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast them out from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

R.20: All this happened to Jerusalem and Judah because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with them, until at last {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} threw them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

decisions.choice: because of Yahweh's anger it came to be: the events of Zedekiah's reign happened through Yahweh's anger
alternatives: Yahweh's anger was against Jerusalem and Judah
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject, and the sentence means that what happened in Jerusalem and Judah, the evil of its kings and the disaster that followed, came about through Yahweh's anger. It may also be read "Yahweh's anger came upon Jerusalem and Judah", with the anger itself as the subject; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: cast them out from before his face: sent them into exile out of his presence
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, to be put away from Yahweh's face is to lose the land where he had made his presence known. The same was said of Israel (17:20). Its completion is told in chapter 25.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon: Jeremiah 52:3; 2 Chronicles 36:13
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:3 has the same words. 2 Chronicles 36:13 adds that Nebuchadnezzar had made him swear by God, and Ezekiel 17:13-15 calls the rebellion the breaking of a covenant oath. The rebellion leads to the siege of 25:1.

decisions.choice: all this
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "it came to be" has no stated subject; Balanced and Readable supply "all this", meaning the evil and disaster just told. Readable turns "the anger of the LORD" into "the LORD was angry with them" and adds "at last" for "until".
